findings: The hall roof now has a visibly sloped blue-gray tile plane instead of a shallow horizontal band.
A concrete modeling defect was fixed: long straight main-hall rafters penetrated the concave roof skin. Sixteen short segments now follow each curved rafter below the tiles.
Pagoda roofs are taller and windows warmer; reduced ambient fill separates warm recessed timber from cool overcast sky.
Foreground overhead framing, camera, near column and gold fitting transforms were retained.
Rain rings are finer and smaller; wet-stone aggregate, film coverage and specular coating were darkened/broken up.
remainingGaps: The foreground still reads as broad smooth slabs, with excessive coherent amber bands; photographic wet-stone texture is not reached.
Foliage still exposes repeated dense horizontal canopy forms and simplified terrain.
Stone lantern shape/material, pagoda proportions, front doorway details and bridge construction remain far from the photograph.
This is an actual 3D draft improvement, not photographic acceptance.
